MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 27, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell at
5:00 p.m., on June 27, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 22, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with legal Counsel: Threat to Public Services or Facilities; Consultation
  with City Attorney and Director of Information Technology David Meyer

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:05 pm with all City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  June 27, 2023
 City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received information, but that no
reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim July 2023 as Parks and Recreation Month

  Presented proclamation to Director Mark Nix.

P2. Presentation by Be Well Orange County

  Received presentation from Vice President Kathryn Hamel, Ph.D. from Be Well OC.

P3. Legislative Update

  Received presentation from Vice President Cori Takkinen from Townsend Public Affairs.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Commented on the budget in regards to making the city a greener place to
live. Suggested for the budget the development of a comprehensive Climate Action Plan, develop a
master plan to convert its fleet to electric vehicles, and to construct charging stations. Recommended
that the City join the Orange County Power Authority. He commended the City on the Housing
Element being presented this evening. Asked for more clarification and transparency on the Core
Vision Plan.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Stated the potential parking garage for Nadadores events is unnecessary and
that the City could use the same transportation we use for special events from City Hall to the
Nadadores facility.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke on the Stop the Monster and voiced concerns on the power of elected
officials being taken away by Sacramento. Supports the Housing Element and voiced concern on
design standards that need to be in place before July 2.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Gave a thank-you to the following, Attorney Curley, Western Waste
Management, Librarians for the LGBTQ+ book display at the Library for Pride Month, Elaine Lister
for the Housing Element, and the Planning & Transportation Commission. Lastly, she thanked
Council Member Vasquez for her leadership in sponsoring two events showing support of LGBTQ+
community as well as her insistence that the Council set priorities for the 23/25 budget.

Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Thanked Director Lister for the Housing Element Workshop which was very
informative. Asked questions regarding the traffic on the La Paz bridge and the syncing of the traffic
lights.
City Council Minutes  2  June 27, 2023
 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Commented and criticized the Respondent’s Brief and cited from the brief
filed by Attorney Aaron Hand and criticized the City Attorney on her June 23, 2020 comments and
stated that they were taken out of context to fit a false narrative and were not properly transcribed.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 10 and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular city Council Meeting of June 13, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated June 2, 2023 in the Amount of $891,560.47

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated June 9, 2023 in the Amount of $566,520.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated June 2, 2023 in the Amount of $218,358.50

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated June 9, 2023 in the Amount of $4,305.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  FY 2023/24 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development Financing
  Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 23-01 Adopting a Budget for the 2023/24 Fiscal Year.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year 2023/24

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 23-01 Adopting a Budget for FY 2023/24.

City Council Minutes  3  June 27, 2023
 8.  Cooperation Agreement (CDBG Funds Transfer) between the City and Housing
  Authority; and First Amendment to Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement
  (Phase IV) Between the Housing Authority and Families Forward

  (1) Adopted Joint Resolution of the City Council and Housing Authority 23-23 Approving
  the First Amendment to Cooperation Agreement (CDBG Funds Transfer) Between the City
  and Housing Authority for Transfer of an Additional $200,000 (for a cumulative total of
  $639,000) of CDBG Funds to Implement the Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement
  (Phase IV) and Making Certain Other Findings, and (2) adopted Housing Authority Resolution
  23-02 Approving the First Amendment to Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement
  (Phase IV) Between the Housing Authority and Families Forward Related to a CDBG Loan of
  up to $639,000 Sourced Solely from CDBG Funds as Transferred by the City to the Housing
  Authority for Acquisition and Long Term Operation of One Single-Family Home for Lease
  and Occupancy by Low Income Persons and Families who are Homeless or at Risk of
  Homelessness, and Making Certain Other Findings.

9.  Establish an Appropriation Limit for the 2023-24 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 23-24 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2023-24 Fiscal Year.

11. Fifth Amendment to Agreement with Matrix Imaging for Document Scanning Services.

  (1) Approved Fifth Amendment to Agreement with Matrix Imaging for an additional $40,000,
  for a total not-to-exceed amount of $166,300, and extend the term of the agreement through
  December 31, 2023 for Document Scanning Services; and (2) adopted Resolution 23-25
  Amending the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget for Costs Related to Document Imaging.

12. Agreement Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program Consultation and
  Implementation

  Approved agreement for Housing Rehabilitation Program Consultation and Implementation
  Services with Theresa Dobbs (A23-34) from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025, in an amount not
  to exceed $60,000 ($30,000 /year).

13. Proposed Lease Submitted by Dish Wireless in Conjunction with a New Wireless
  Telecommunication Facility on an Existing 83-Foot-Tall Light Standard Located at the
  World Cup (Potocki) Soccer Fields at 27301 La Paz Road

  Approved and Authorized the City Manager to Execute the Lease with Dish Wireless (A23-
  35).

14. Agreement for Professional Services for Community Development Block Grant Program
  Administration

  Approved Agreement for Community Development Block Grant Administration Services with
  Mike Linares, Inc. (A23-36) from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025, in an amount not to exceed
  $110,500.
City Council Minutes  4  June 27, 2023
 15. MV Shuttle Services

  Approved the Fourth Amendment with LAZ Parking California, Inc. for the operation of the
  MV Shuttle contingent upon adoption of the FY 2023-2024 Operating Budget.

16. Annual Maintenance Program for Plumbing and Related Services at City Facilities

  (1) Awarded a contract to Santa Margarita Plumbing and Air, Inc. (A23-37) for the Annual
  Maintenance Program for Plumbing and Related Services for the period of July 1, 2023 to June
  30, 2025 in an amount not to exceed $270,000.00; and (2) authorized the issuance of a purchase
  order to Santa Margarita Plumbing and Air, Inc. for the period July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024,
  in amount not to exceed $135,000.00, pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget
  by the City Council.

18. Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs (A23-38) for
  State legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed the
  amount of $120,000 for the period of July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10. Sober living Task-Force Comprehensive Management Assistance

  Council Member Vasquez asked for clarification on how much the City has spent to date on this
  task force, if we are the only City spending money on this, and has the ACCOC given any
  indication when they will step in.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that we have spent between $37,000-$40,000. He stated at
  this point no other cities have put money toward this effort, and that the ACCOC has not
  specified a timeline when they will take over. He stated that they hope to look into discussing
  with other cities to assist in paying.

  Council Member Bucknum shared that the idea of sharing costs has been discussed at the task
  force and it will be continued at the next two meetings. She explained that the difference
  between the Task Force and the ACCOC, is that the ACCOC is elected officials only. She
  stated that having public members that are being impacted by this on the task force makes the
  legislature look at it more seriously.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to award
  a contract with Venture Strategic (A23-33) in the amount of $60,000.00 for continuing
  Comprehensive Management Assistance of the newly formed Sober Living Task-force.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
City Council Minutes  5  June 27, 2023
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17. Annual Maintenance Program for Pool Maintenance Related Services at City Facilities

  Council Member Vasquez asked for clarification on the contract amount.

  Director of Public Services explained that the City has two contracts, one with 1st Choice that
  provides daily maintenance to the pools, and another contract for the purchase of pool
  chemicals which is the contract we are having an issue with. That distributor does not want to
  hold to his cost. He stated that it has been difficult to set up a bid with a distributor to lock in
  a cost. This amendment for 1st Choice is to have them purchase the pool chemicals and pass on
  the cost to the City with no mark-up.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Goodell, to (1) approve
  Seventh Amendment to the existing pool maintenance contract with 1st Choice Pool & Spa
  Solutions for the subject services for the period of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2025 in the
  amount of $520,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a change order to 1st Choice Pool & Spa
  Solutions for the period of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed
  $260,000.00 pending the adoption of the 2023-2025 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARING

19. General Plan Amendment GPA2021-35 - Revision to City-Initiated Petition Related to
  the City’s Housing Element Update as Required by State Law to Address the State’s 6th
  Housing Cycle for the Years 2021-2029

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Mayor Goodell opened the Public Hearing at 7:48 pm

  Cathy Palmer, MV: Thanked Elaine Lister and her staff on the Housing Element. Encouraged
  entry level housing in the forms of condominiums and townhomes with 3 and 4 bedroom units.

  Peggy O’Neill, MV: Thanked Elaine Lister and her staff on the Housing Element and for the
  housing workshop. She hopes the city is ready to support developers. Encouraged the
  inclusionary housing ordinance to guarantee that affordable housing will be built.

  Stacy Holmes, MV: Stated the housing workshop was very informative. He says we have to
  care about the homeless and caring about the issues and these sites have developers for low
  income housing and he hopes the City reaches out to these developers.
City Council Minutes  6  June 27, 2023
   Rona Henry, Laguna Woods: Spoke in support of an inclusionary ordinance. She outlined the
  City of Irvine’s inclusionary ordinance very low, low and extremely housing.

  Ken Kisling, MV: Supports the housing element and outlined his thoughts on the plan.

  Carlos Pianelli, MV: Appreciated the efforts of Elaine Lister and her staff. Stated there should
  be a 15% minimum of affordable housing in developments.

  Mayor Goodell closed the Public Hearing at 8:06 pm.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to direct
  staff to make additional clean-up and revision to the Housing Element based on recent
  communication with the California Department of Housing and Community Development
  (HCD) and submit to HCD for review.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

20. Adoption of the 2023-2025 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services presented the staff report.

  She stated that there are 3 additional changes based on our meeting with Council Member
  Vasquez yesterday.

  Restating the third City Council objective to: Continue to facilitate the growth of Mission
  Viejo’s sports economy by maintaining the Mission Viejo Sports Tourism website, presenting
  what Mission Viejo has to offer to both national and international athletes. Partner with the
  Orange County Sports Commission to build a greater national and international sports presence.
  Obtain a City-specific Economic Study to identify and facilitate positive economic impact and
  growth. Page 90
  Add a performance measure for Community Development that reports on the number of
  applications received under the Housing Rehabilitation loan program. Page 179

  Add information in the City Manager budget message to document budget items not included
  in the final 23-25 budget. Among other items, this list will include mention of park playground
  rehabilitation projects, North Oso Creek Bike Pedestrian Trail Open Space project and slope
  rehabilitation funding. Page 10 and 11.

City Council Minutes  7  June 27, 2023
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Addressed concerns of the vision plan and that the parking garage was
  not part of this plan. She commented that there is no money for playground equipment, shade
  structures and that the landscape budge has been severely cut. She criticized the Mayor and
  the Council that these vision plans are not obtainable.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 23-26 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2023-25 and
  Appropriating Funds for the FY 2023/24 only; and (2) adopt Resolution 23-27 Amending the
  City's salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule Effective July 1, 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

21. Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 23-28 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

23. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Ruesch.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon gave a brief report on the northerly trail head at Casta del
Sol where the idea is to make it a more gradual incline for bike and pedestrians safety. He outlined
the opportunity the City has by working with the Contractor of the La Paz Widening Project in

City Council Minutes  8  June 27, 2023
 hauling dirt. The contractor would give us a cost credit for this project by taking the dirt to the trail
head.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum stated that she has been out of town attending a family member’s
celebration of life. She announced that this Friday June 30, there will be a free concert on the Village
Green by Pop Vision. Council Member Bucknum reminded residents of the 4th of July Street Faire
and enjoy the local display booths and enjoy the fireworks.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch announced that last week the first human typhus was detected in Mission
Viejo in the area of the 241 Toll Road and Los Alisos. He stated so far it has been contained. He
stated that there is a low mosquito attendance but be aware of standing water.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated that she attended her first ribbon cutting for the Platonic Beauty
Salon of off Alicia and Via Fabricante. She also attended the Poetry and Art Reception at the Mission
Viejo Library and stated that the turnout was great.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that she was in Washington DC for her husband’s reunion of his
Officer’s Training Class and had a wonderful time. She attended the South Orange Amateur Radio
Association (SOARA) which is a group of amateur radio people that set up a 24-hour display and
actual training in Gilleran Park. She explained that the function of this group is in the event of a
disaster they will be able to communicate with their ham radios. The City supports them and
appreciates the service and resources they provide. Council Member Kelley also attended the
Montanoso Open House. Lastly, she spoke about the fencing at schools that are adjoined to parks
and indicated that she signed her grandchildren up for the Summer Reading Program at the Library.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that the attended the Home Burglary & Prevention Seminar at the Norman P.
Murray Center. It was well attended with helpful information. He had breakfast with
Congresswoman Young Kim and other Mayors in her district. Mayor Goodell said met with the
Sports Tourism Consultant Greg Harney and Australian Professional Rugby Representative Brendon
City Council Minutes  9  June 27, 2023
 Morris for a tour of our facilities. He also toured a Cricket Sports Group through our facilities. He
stated he attended the Elks Lodge Flag Day Ceremony. Mayor Goodell also attended the ACCOC
newest affordable housing development called the Finamore Place Project in Anaheim, as well as
the OCCOG Board of Directors Meeting. Lastly, he stated the Poetry and Art Reception at the
Library.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 9:23 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 11, 2023, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________
 Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 11, 2023

City Council Minutes  10  June 27, 2023
